nodes.summary: The executable checker is correct for all initial infinite model runs.
nodes.title: Correctness of the executable LTL model checker

nodes.summary: Full-LTL checking by the existing finite Büchi reachability algorithm. The finite/decidable data requirements are only for execution, not recognition.

nodes.summary: The finite-state product for runs that violate the full LTL formula.
nodes.title: Counterexample product for an LTL formula

nodes.summary: For every LTL formula $\varphi$ and every valuation of its atoms on the input letters, some nondeterministic Büchi automaton with at most $4^{|\varphi|}$ states accepts exactly the infinite words that satisfy $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Vardi–Wolper translation with an exponential state bound

nodes.summary: For every LTL formula $\varphi$ and every valuation of its atoms on the input letters, some finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton accepts exactly the infinite words that satisfy $\varphi$. Neither the atoms nor the alphabet need be finite or decidable.
nodes.title: Every LTL formula has a finite-state Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: Structural fairness is exactly generalized Büchi acceptance.
nodes.title: Tableau fairness is generalized Büchi acceptance

nodes.summary: Every until occurrence is absent or fulfilled at arbitrarily late times.
nodes.title: Fairness of a tableau annotation sequence

nodes.summary: Equivalently, every adjacent state pair has a real model transition.
nodes.title: Runs are sequences with a transition between adjacent states

nodes.summary: An initial infinite state run, witnessed by a canonical action execution.
nodes.title: Initial infinite run of a transition system

nodes.summary: Exact omega-language equality for the generalized tableau.
nodes.title: Generalized LTL tableau language equals the formula language

nodes.summary: Every LTL formula has precisely its existing language as a Büchi language.
nodes.title: Büchi automaton language equals the LTL formula language

nodes.summary: The full tableau recognizes exactly the existing LTL satisfaction relation.
nodes.title: LTL tableau accepts exactly the satisfying words

nodes.summary: The ordinary Büchi recognizer accepts exactly satisfaction of the formula.
nodes.title: Büchi automaton accepts exactly the satisfying words

nodes.summary: A counterexample word is exactly an infinite model run violating LTL.
nodes.title: Counterexample words are runs violating the formula

nodes.summary: Membership exposes exactly the initial, local, and fairness conditions.
nodes.title: Tableau acceptance via initial, local and fairness conditions

nodes.summary: A product accepts precisely the model runs accepted by its recognizer.
nodes.title: Product accepts exactly the runs accepted by the recognizer

nodes.summary: An infinite sequence of states is accepted by the Büchi automaton of a transition system iff it is an initial infinite run of the system: $L_\omega(A_P)$ is the set of computations of $P$.
nodes.title: The language of the system automaton is the set of runs

nodes.summary: All initial infinite runs of a transition system satisfy an LTL formula $\varphi$ iff $L_\omega(A_P) \cap L_\omega(A_{\neg\varphi}) = \emptyset$.
nodes.title: LTL model checking is emptiness of an intersection

nodes.summary: Universal infinite-run satisfaction is emptiness of the counterexample language.
nodes.title: LTL satisfaction iff the counterexample language is empty

nodes.summary: All initial infinite runs of a transition system satisfy an LTL formula $\varphi$ iff $L_\omega(A_P) \subseteq L_\omega(A_\varphi)$, where $A_P$ is the Büchi automaton of the system and $A_\varphi$ the Büchi automaton of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: LTL model checking is language inclusion

nodes.summary: Full-LTL model checking reduces to the proved finite Büchi lasso criterion. A cycle must be nonempty; neither seriality nor finite action/atom types are needed.
nodes.title: Finite-model LTL satisfaction iff no counterexample lasso

nodes.summary: All initial infinite canonical executions satisfy the formula.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an LTL formula by all initial runs

nodes.summary: The nondeterministic Büchi automaton of an LTL formula $\varphi$, obtained by degeneralizing its tableau, has at most $4^{|\varphi|} = 2^{2|\varphi|}$ states.
nodes.title: Exponential state bound for the Büchi automaton of an LTL formula

nodes.summary: The truth-annotation tableau of an LTL formula $\varphi$ has exactly $2^{|\varphi|}$ states: a state assigns one truth value to each syntactic occurrence in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Exact state count of the LTL tableau

nodes.summary: The computable update is exactly the existing generic degeneralization.
nodes.title: Computable counter update equals generic degeneralization

nodes.summary: The number of until occurrences of an LTL formula $\varphi$, which is the number of generalized Büchi acceptance sets of its tableau, is strictly less than $|\varphi|$: every formula has at least one atom or truth leaf, which is not an until.
nodes.title: Fairness obligations are fewer than the formula size

nodes.summary: The number of until occurrences, hence of fairness requirements.
nodes.title: Number of until fairness obligations

nodes.summary: The Boolean test for each until fairness requirement.
nodes.title: Boolean test for an until fairness obligation

nodes.summary: Every LTL formula has size at least $1$.
nodes.title: Formulas have positive size

nodes.summary: Synchronized state-reading product, with the recognizer's Büchi condition.
nodes.title: Product of a transition system with a Büchi recognizer

nodes.summary: The executable test returns `true` exactly on satisfiable formulas.
nodes.title: Correctness of the executable satisfiability test

nodes.summary: For a finite alphabet and a decidable valuation, this Boolean runs the Büchi emptiness test on the automaton of the formula, which has at most $4^{|\varphi|}$ states, and returns `true` when the automaton is nonempty. No running time is proved.
nodes.title: Executable LTL satisfiability test

nodes.summary: An LTL formula is satisfiable iff its Büchi automaton has an accepting state that is reachable from an initial state and lies on a nonempty cycle. With the lasso word of that cycle, a satisfiable formula has an ultimately periodic model $u v^\omega$ (not stated separately here).
nodes.title: LTL satisfiability by the lasso criterion

nodes.summary: An LTL formula is satisfiable iff its Büchi automaton accepts some infinite word. This is the reduction in Vardi's proof of Theorem 24 (Sistla and Clarke: LTL satisfiability is PSPACE-complete); only the reduction is formalized here, not the complexity bound.
nodes.title: LTL satisfiability is Büchi nonemptiness

nodes.summary: An LTL formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable, for a valuation of its atoms on the letters, if some infinite word satisfies $\varphi$. With letters the sets of atoms read by membership, this is the satisfiability of Vardi's Section 4.1.
nodes.title: Satisfiable LTL formula

nodes.summary: The size $|\varphi|$ of an LTL formula is the number of nodes of its syntax tree: atoms and truth count $1$, negation and next add $1$, and conjunction and until add $1$ to the sizes of their two arguments.
nodes.title: Size of an LTL formula

nodes.summary: One Boolean for each syntactic occurrence in an LTL formula.
nodes.title: Truth-annotation states of the LTL tableau

nodes.summary: Local equations at every occurrence. The symbol labels the source state.
nodes.title: Local transition relation of the LTL tableau

nodes.summary: The Büchi automaton $A_P$ of a transition system with initial states $I$ has the states of the system as states and as letters, $I$ as initial states, and a transition from $s$ to $t$ reading $s$ whenever the system has a transition from $s$ to $t$; every state is accepting, so every infinite run is accepting.
nodes.title: Büchi automaton of a transition system

nodes.summary: An LTL formula is valid iff its negation is not satisfiable.
nodes.title: Validity is unsatisfiability of the negation

nodes.summary: An LTL formula $\varphi$ is valid, for a valuation of its atoms on the letters, if every infinite word satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Valid LTL formula

nodes.summary: The truth bit at the root of an annotation.
nodes.title: Root truth bit of a tableau annotation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
